title: Reading Comprehension
intro: Reading comprehension gives a passage and several questions on it. Unlike vocabulary or grammar, the answers are all in front of you — the skill is locating and interpreting them under time pressure. The reliable method: skim the passage for its gist, read the questions, then scan back for the specific lines that answer each one. Crucially, answer from the passage, not your own knowledge or opinion.

items.name: Skim first
items.formula: get the main idea before the questions

items.name: Answer from the text
items.formula: never from outside knowledge or opinion

items.name: Locate the line
items.formula: scan back to the exact sentence for detail questions

items.name: Eliminate
items.formula: reject options that overstate or are not stated

topics.name: Main Idea & Title
topics.details: Main-idea and title questions ask what the whole passage is about, not one detail. The answer covers the entire passage — not too broad and not too narrow. The opening/closing sentences and any repeated theme point to it.

solved.problem: What does a "main idea" answer have to cover?
solved.solution: The whole passage — not one detail and not a vague generality.

solved.problem: Where do clues to the main idea usually sit?
solved.solution: The opening and closing sentences and any repeated theme.

solved.problem: Why reject a "too narrow" title option?
solved.solution: It covers only one detail/paragraph, not the whole passage.

solved.problem: Should the title come from outside knowledge?
solved.solution: No — it must reflect the passage itself.

unsolved.problem: A good title is neither too broad nor too ___.
The main idea should reflect the ___ passage.
An option restating only one example is too ___.
Repeated themes across paragraphs hint at the ___.
Should the main idea include your opinion?

topics.name: Inference & Tone
topics.details: Inference questions ask what the passage implies but doesn't state — the answer must be strongly supported, a small logical step. Tone questions ask the author's attitude (critical, appreciative, neutral, sarcastic), judged from word choices.

solved.problem: A valid inference must be ___ by the passage.
solved.solution: Strongly supported (a small logical step, not a guess).

solved.problem: How do you judge the author's tone?
solved.solution: From the writer's word choices and attitude.
They overstate unless the passage is clearly that strong.

solved.problem: Is an inference directly stated in the text?
solved.solution: No — it is implied but well-supported.

unsolved.problem: An inference is implied, not directly ___.
A mocking, cutting tone is called?
A balanced, fact-only tone is?
A tone praising the subject is?
An inference must be ___ by the text.

topics.name: Vocabulary in Context
topics.details: These ask the meaning of a word AS USED in the passage, which may differ from its common meaning. Read the full sentence and replace the word with each option to see which keeps the sense.

solved.problem: How do you find a word's meaning in context?
solved.solution: Read the sentence and substitute each option to keep the sense.

solved.problem: "Novel" can mean a book or ___ depending on context.
Should you use the most common meaning automatically?
solved.solution: No — the passage's use decides the meaning.

solved.problem: What helps disambiguate a word's sense?

unsolved.problem: In "a fine for parking", "fine" means a ___.
"He will address the issue" — "address" means to ___.
Context for word meaning comes from the ___.
"A current of air" — "current" means a ___.
Replace the word with each option to test the ___.

topics.name: Detail & Fact Questions
topics.details: Detail questions ask for a fact explicitly stated ('According to the passage, …'). Scan back to the relevant line and match it. Beware options that are true in real life but not stated, and options that distort the wording.

solved.problem: Where is the answer to a detail question found?
solved.solution: Explicitly in the passage — scan back to the line.

solved.problem: Why reject a "true but not stated" option?
solved.solution: Detail answers must come from the passage, not general knowledge.

solved.problem: What does the correct detail option do?

unsolved.problem: A detail answer is ___ stated in the passage.
An option true in life but absent from the text should be?
The best detail option ___ the line accurately.
To answer, ___ back to the relevant sentence.
"According to the passage" signals a ___ question.

shortcuts: Skim for the gist, read the questions, then scan back for specifics.
Answer ONLY from the passage — never from outside knowledge or opinion.
Main idea covers the whole passage (not too broad, not too narrow).
Inference = small supported step; tone = author's word choices.
For vocabulary-in-context, substitute each option into the sentence.
mistakes: Answering from general knowledge instead of the passage.
Choosing a detail that is true in life but not stated.
Picking a too-broad or too-narrow main idea/title.
Over-inferring beyond what the text supports.
pyq: SSC usually sets one passage with 4–5 questions mixing main idea, inference, vocabulary-in-context and detail. Skim-then-scan and "answer from the text" are the whole technique.
summary: Reading comprehension is locating and interpreting, not recalling. Skim for the gist, read the questions, scan back for the exact lines, and answer strictly from the passage. Match main-idea options to the whole passage, keep inferences well-supported, and read words in their passage context.
